diary.endbound_ember.zombie:
X/X, Sunny
Went mushroom-picking in the woods with Dad today. I found a HUGE brown mushroom! Mom made mushroom soup for dinner. It smelled sooo good.

X/X, Rain
Monsters came to the village. Dad hid me in the cellar and told me not to make a sound. It's so loud outside. I'm scared.

I don't know how long I slept. When I woke up, I didn't need to eat anymore, and the cold didn't bother me. The girl in the mirror... is she still me?

There's always a sky full of stars in my dreams, and their light feels warm on my skin. I sat on a stone at the village gate and watched the sky brighten, and suddenly I wanted Mom's mushroom soup more than anything.

diary.endbound_ember.zombie_forest:
X/X, Sunny
Went deep into the forest alone to gather herbs today. The sunlight broke into little pieces through the leaves. So beautiful. I even saw a deer!

X/X, Overcast
Monsters surrounded me on the way back. I ran as hard as I could, but there were just so many of them... I couldn't get away...

After being bitten, I had a fever for a long time. When I woke up, the wound had already healed, but... something felt different. My eyes got really bright, and I could see clearly even at night.

I can still recognize the little path back to the forest. One day, if someone is willing to walk it with me, I'd like to see that grove where the sunlight breaks into pieces again.

diary.endbound_ember.zombie_plague:
X/X, Sunny
People in the village started getting sick, one after another. Mom said it's fine, but her hands were shaking. I helped her brew medicine, hoping it would help.

X/X, Rain
I caught it too. The fever wouldn't go down, and Dad locked me in my room, saying I could come out when I was better. It's so quiet outside the window, not a single person.

The fever broke, but I don't feel hungry anymore. The door had been nailed shut from the outside. I pried the boards off and walked out — the village was completely empty.

The starry sky is so beautiful. I sat on the roof and waited for so long, and still no one came back. In the end I decided I should walk on by myself, and see what else is out there.

diary.endbound_ember.drowned:
X/X, Sunny
Beat my brother in a swimming race again! He says one day I'll swim across the big river beyond the village.

X/X, Storm
The boat is rocking so hard. Seawater keeps pouring over the deck. It's so cold... colder than the river in winter...

I lay at the bottom of the sea for so long. Strangely, I don't need to breathe anymore. The stars in my dreams kept me company, like little lanterns.

(The writing is blurred by water) I want to go home and see everyone... but looking like this, would they even recognize me? In the end I still turned my face toward the village.

diary.endbound_ember.drowned_river:
X/X, Sunny
Played in the river with my friends today. The water was so cold! I caught a tiny fish! Let it go though, it was so little.

X/X, Rain
The river had risen so much. I slipped and fell right in, the current was so fast. I thrashed desperately but couldn't grab onto the rocks by the bank.

After I sank, I thought I'd be terrified, but the bottom of the river was so quiet. I didn't need to breathe anymore. Waterweeds tangled around my fingers like hair.

(The writing runs and blurs) I drifted so far along the river. Moonlight spilled into the water, so beautiful. I want to follow this river back to where we used to play.

diary.endbound_ember.drowned_fog:
X/X, Fog
Went fishing at the dock with Grandpa at dawn. The fog was so thick you couldn't see anything, only hear the sound of waves.

X/X, Fog
I was walking along the dock and slipped — the water was so cold, it rushed right in. I tried to call for Grandpa, but when I opened my mouth it was all water.

I walked along the bottom for so long. After I stopped needing to breathe, the ocean felt so peaceful. Lights flickered under the thick fog, like someone was waving.

(The paper is torn) I can see the reef where Grandpa fishes, right there below the water. I'll stay here and wait for him to come fishing again.

diary.endbound_ember.survivor:
X/X, Rain
Chased by skeletons and spiders to a dead end, a zombie appeared ahead. I thought I was done for. But she suddenly turned and shoved the skeleton away, then growled at the spider — she was saving me.

X/X, Overcast
She brought me back to her camp. There were other zombies there. I was terrified, but they just looked at me curiously — one even handed me a piece of bread. They were kind to me, nothing like monsters.

X/X, Sunny
After a few days at the camp, they escorted me back to the village. I told the villagers that not all undead are monsters, some still retain reason and kindness — but no one believed me.

They said I was in shock and hallucinating. But I remember those gentle eyes, and the hand that gave me bread. One day I'll make them believe it too.

diary.endbound_ember.survivor_observe:
X/X, Sunny
Got lost. It was getting dark and I couldn't find my way back. A drowned crawled out of the river. I backed away in fear, but she just looked at me, then pointed in a direction — toward the village.

X/X, Overcast
I followed her direction. She stayed behind me the whole time, like an escort. When we ran into a creeper, she rushed forward and pushed it away — she got blown up herself.

X/X, Rain
At the village entrance, she stopped and didn't follow in. I looked back at her. She waved at me, then turned and walked into the darkness. I went looking for her the next day, but never saw her again.

I told the village chief about this. He said it was just coincidence. But I know what I saw. I'll keep searching until I find her again.

diary.endbound_ember.survivor_resonance:
X/X, Overcast
I had a fever, lying in the wild unable to move. A zombie found me. I thought she'd bite me, but she just crouched down and covered me with her tattered cloak.

X/X, Rain
She stayed by my side the whole time, driving away monsters that approached. At dawn she led me to a water source and picked berries, placing them beside me. She cared for me for three days.

X/X, Sunny
The fever broke and I could walk. She escorted me near the village then left. I ran back and told everyone a zombie saved and cared for me — they thought the fever scrambled my brain.

No one believes a zombie would save a person. But I still hold that torn cloak, still warm from her body. The world is more complex than we think — don't be quick to swing your sword.

diary.endbound_ember.survivor_heal:
X/X, Overcast
Got my leg blown up by a creeper, hiding in an abandoned house waiting to die. A zombie pushed the door open. I closed my eyes. But she didn't attack — she turned and left.

X/X, Sunny
She came back, holding herbs — plants that can stop bleeding. She clumsily crushed the herbs, applied them to my wound, and wrapped it with torn cloth.

X/X, Rain
Under her care, the wound didn't get infected. She came every day to change the dressing, sometimes bringing food. After a week I could walk. She watched me leave, standing at the door seeing me off.

When I got back to the village I told them about this. The blacksmith mocked me, saying zombies can't possibly know herbs. But those bandaging techniques — someone clearly taught her that. She was once human too.

diary.endbound_ember.zombie_mine:
X/X, Sunny
Went with the villagers to dig in the mine today. Where the torchlight fell, the stone sparkled. It was pretty.

X/X, Overcast
The tunnel caved in. My companion and I were buried together. Pitch dark, I could see nothing, and all I could hear was my own heartbeat.

Something in the dark bit me. When I opened my eyes again, my companion was gone. I was not hungry. I was not in pain.

I dug toward the wind for a long, long time and finally saw the light above ground again. I'll keep waiting, for my companion to come walking out of that tunnel.

diary.endbound_ember.zombie_cave:
X/X, Sunny
Sneaked into the cave behind the village today. So exciting! The cave was cool, and glowing little bugs crawled along the walls.

X/X, Overcast
My torch burned out and I got lost among the forking tunnels. As I felt my way along the rock, something bit me from behind.

When I woke up, it was strange — the cave was pitch black, yet I could see everything clearly.

I followed the draft from the cave mouth for a long time before I crawled back to the surface. I can see things others cannot now, but I still want to go back to where there are torches.

diary.endbound_ember.zombie_siege:
X/X, Rain
The monsters came to besiege the village. I stood behind the wooden fence with the grown-ups, still gripping a wooden club.

X/X, Rain
A zombie bit my shoulder from behind. It hurt so much. But I couldn't run — if I ran, the village would fall. I held on until dawn.

Dawn came, and the village held. But I began to feel cold, and my favorite roast chicken... tasted different.

Dawn came and the village held, yet I began to feel cold. I don't regret standing there until morning — someone had to hold the fence.

diary.endbound_ember.drowned_reef:
X/X, Sunny
Today I dived to the deep sea with the uncle who gathers coral. The coral was beautiful — red and purple, like a garden under the water.

X/X, Overcast
Weed caught my ankle and I couldn't pull free. Something pale dragged me into a deeper crevice among the rocks...

(the ink is fading) When I woke, there was only coral and fish swimming around me. It seems I no longer need to breathe.

I lived in that crevice for a long, long time and learned to avoid the big fish, but I never found the way up. The sea isn't as frightening as I thought — only a little lonely.

diary.endbound_ember.drowned_well:
X/X, Sunny
Went to the old well at the village gate for water. The rope was so worn. I cranked it while thinking of hurrying home.

X/X, Overcast
The rope snapped. The bucket fell and took me with it. The well water was so cold. I tried to grab the wall but I couldn't.

I soaked for a long, long time before I woke. My skin had turned cool, yet it gripped the well wall without slipping.

I climbed back to the surface, and the village was so quiet, as if it did not know me. Even so, I want to go and look at that old well every day.

X/X, Snow
The river finally froze over! My friends and I agreed to skate on the ice, and whoever fell first would buy the candy.

X/X, Snow
The ice split open. The moment I fell into the hole, it was so cold I could not even cry out.

(my handwriting is shaking) After the cold numbed everything, I... no longer needed to breathe. I looked up through the ice, and the sunlight came down in patches.

I waited until spring before I floated up from under the ice. When the river opened, the wind touched my face, and I suddenly remembered everyone laughing last winter.

diary.endbound_ember.survivor_explore:
X/X, Sunny
Today I sneaked into those abandoned ruins. It was dark and damp, and strange patterns covered the walls.

X/X, Overcast
Oh no — a pack of monsters surrounded me, and my way back was blocked. I was sure I would never get out.

X/X, Sunny
A Zombie Girl saved me. She lured the monsters away and took several hits herself. By the time I came to my senses, she was gone.

Back in the village, I said I would write them down, and the villagers all said I had gone mad. Still, I recorded everything I saw in the ruins. Why would the undead save a human? I want to understand.

X/X, Rain
When the monsters rushed into the village, I was inside telling my little sister a story. Fire spread along the roof beams.

X/X, Rain
The door was blocked from outside, and the smoke stung my eyes shut. I thought my sister and I would burn together in there.

Then someone smashed the door open — not a villager, but a Zombie Girl. She dragged me out, and her own arm caught the flames.

By dawn the village had saved only half its people. I packed my things and left. I want to see where the undead actually live.

X/X, Rain
When the monsters rushed into the village, I was inside telling my little sister a story. Fire spread along the roof beams.

X/X, Rain
The door was blocked from outside, and the smoke stung my eyes shut. I thought my sister and I would burn together in there.
Then someone smashed the door open — not a villager, but a Zombie Girl. She dragged me out, and her own arm caught the flames.
By dawn the village had saved only half its people. I packed my things and left. I want to see where the undead actually live.
diary.endbound_ember.survivor_wander:
X/X, Sunny
I walked in the wilderness for three days. My rations were long gone and my ankle was sprained. Night was coming, and I could not even find water.

X/X, Overcast
I slumped against a rock and waited to die. Half-conscious, I felt something cold touch my hand.

When I woke, two fish lay beside me, and a grey figure in the distance was leading me forward. She was the one who brought me to water.

I survived. Since that day, I have never seen the undead as mere monsters again. Once I have my strength back, I'm going to find that grey figure.

diary.endbound_ember.healed.zombie.page4: When the starlight settled on me it wasn't hot at all — it seeped in slowly, like warm water. For the first time my body felt warm. Thank you for pulling me out of that cold.
diary.endbound_ember.healed.zombie_fores: When the light swept across my eyes, I could suddenly see the color of sunlight again. Thank you for making me the girl who gets lost in the woods once more.
diary.endbound_ember.healed.zombie_plagu: The healing light felt like a gentle spring rain that didn't burn. The sickly smell faded from my skin bit by bit. Thank you for letting me deserve the village again.
The starlight slipped into my wounds so lightly, as if someone whispered that it was all right. Thank you for truly bringing me back above ground.
When the light poured in, the darkness fled far away — and I wasn't afraid anymore. Thank you for letting me see daylight again.
diary.endbound_ember.healed.zombie_siege: The healing was so warm it made me sleepy, like someone tucking a blanket around me. Thank you for letting me stand in the sun and guard my home again.
diary.endbound_ember.healed.drowned.page: The starlight that came down through the seawater was warm, and my breath came back with it. Thank you — I can finally go home without hiding from everyone.
diary.endbound_ember.healed.drowned_rive: When the light wrapped around me along the current, it was like someone took my hand. Thank you for leading me from the riverbed all the way back to the bank.
The moment the fog cleared, the light fell warm on my face, and for the first time the sea wind didn't feel cold. Thank you for letting me walk back to Grandpa myself.
diary.endbound_ember.healed.drowned_reef: The starlight dissolved in the water, brightening like coral colors one shade at a time. It was so comfortable. Thank you — I can finally float up to where the sunlight is.
diary.endbound_ember.healed.drowned_well: When the healing light came down, the chill of the well water faded little by little. Thank you — I can finally stand by the well and really look at this village.
The light seeped down through the ice, warm enough to remind me of spring. Thank you for truly saving me from that winter's ice hole.
